text: The Procurement Legislation (“the Procurement Legislation”) referred to in these rules include (but are not limited to) the following: - Public Contract Regulations 2006 (PCR2006) - Public Contract Regulations 2015 (PCR2015) -  Procurement Act 2023 (PA2023) - Procurement Regulations 2024 and Guidance issued by the Cabinet Office
note: Lists the laws the Rules refer to. Nothing is required of anyone, so there is nothing to test.

text: These Rules protect the legal position of the Council in respect of compliance with the law and in its contractual dealings with external suppliers and contractors. They protect the interests of Members, Officers and the citizens of West Berkshire.
note: States what the Rules are for. No obligation.

text: Every purchase, contract or official order for works, supplies or services made by the Council shall be for the purpose of implementing the Council's policies and must be made in accordance with the Council's duties of Best Value, Equality, Sustainable Commissioning and its Social Value Policy.
note: An overarching duty (purchases must serve Council policy and follow Best Value, Equality and Social Value). Auditors test it through the specific controls that implement it, such as the recorded social value consideration in 3.5, not directly.

text: Annexed are Appendices comprising Tables referred to.
note: Points to the appendices.

text: Any contract award with a value over £500,000 is a Key Decision of the Council.
note: An award over £500,000 is a Key Decision. Evidence: the decision record and Forward Plan entry for each award above that value.

text: Where a Service Director does not have delegated authority to enter into a contract, approval in accordance with Appendix A is required before the contract can be awarded.
note: Approval is required BEFORE award where the Service Director lacks authority. Appendix A says who approves; this clause adds the timing, which is testable on its own. Evidence: approval date against award date.

text: any conditions attached by the Executive or the Council to the exercise of powers delegated by them;
note: One item in the list of things purchases must comply with. It names no specific condition, so there is nothing to test unless a particular delegation carries conditions.

text: The financial value thresholds at which processes become mandatory are published on the Procurement intranet page.
note: Says where the threshold values are published.

text: Where a contract is above the relevant Procurement Legislation financial threshold there are two main types of procedure available under PA2023: Open Procedure; and Competitive Flexible Procedure.
note: Describes the two procedures available above the threshold. No obligation.

text: No tender received after the time and date specified for its opening shall be accepted or considered by the Council unless the Monitoring Officer is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances and the other tenders have not been opened.
note: Late tenders must not be accepted unless the Monitoring Officer is satisfied there are exceptional circumstances. Evidence: tender receipt log against the deadline, and the Monitoring Officer's record for any late tender accepted.

text: Tenders subject to the provisions of the Procurement Legislation shall be evaluated in accordance with the legislative provisions. Advice from the Procurement team may be sought on the selection and evaluation criteria.
note: Tenders under the Procurement Legislation shall be evaluated as the legislation requires, which means against the published award criteria. A standard procurement audit test. Evidence: the evaluation record against the criteria in the tender documents. The second sentence (advice may be sought) is optional and not part of the rule.

text: for contracts above the relevant Threshold and up to £500,000, the S.151 Officer will consult with the Monitoring Officer and the appropriate Executive Director provided and an exception report has been approved by the relevant board unless 7.3 applies and for reasons of urgency such prior approval is not possible in which case a report will be supplied retrospectively;
note: Exceptions above the Threshold and up to £500,000: S151 Officer consults, and the board approves an exception report. Lower bound is the statutory Threshold, which the PDF does not state, so it is not checked. Evidence: the exception report and board approval.

text: have had relevant approval sought under these Rules.
note: Every exception or waiver must have had the relevant approval sought. It overlaps with 7.3, 7.4 and 7.5.3, but it is an obligation with evidence: an approval request for each waiver. A rule held at 7.5 also counts.

text: framework arrangements (including those set up by authorised central purchasing bodies such as Crown Commercial Services, other contracting authorities and by the Council itself);
note: One item in the definition of a Purchasing Scheme.

text: Where a Purchasing Scheme is used there shall be a whole or partial exemption from the obligations under these Rules in respect of the choice and conduct of procedures. Advice should be sought from Commissioning and Procurement Team prior to entering to such arrangements.
note: Advice should be sought from the Commissioning and Procurement Team before using a Purchasing Scheme. Worded as "should", but it names a specific action with evidence, so it is tested as expected practice. Evidence: the advice obtained before the scheme was used. The first sentence (an exemption applies) is not a rule.

text: All contracts entered into by the Council as detailed in Appendix B must be in writing in a form approved by the Monitoring Officer or their delegated officer.
note: Contracts must be in writing, in a form approved by the Monitoring Officer. Evidence: the signed contract and the approved form.

text: Where a Standard Form of Agreement is to be amended, the form of contract shall be prepared/amended by the relevant Service Director for approval by the Monitoring Officer or their delegated officer.
note: An amended standard form needs the Monitoring Officer's approval. Evidence: the approval of the amended form.

text: requirements on the contractor to comply with all relevant legislation, including (but not limited to) equalities and health and safety legislation;
note: Every contract shall include, as a minimum, a clause requiring the contractor to comply with legislation. Evidence: the contract itself. A rule held at 10.7 also counts.

text: No relaxation of full indemnities releasing the Council from all liability whether provided by public liability insurance or other instrument shall be allowed unless authorised in writing by the Monitoring Officer and the S.151 Officer or their nominated officers.
note: No relaxation of indemnities without written authorisation from the Monitoring Officer and S151 Officer. Evidence: the written authorisation for any contract with reduced indemnities.

text: The bond must be in a form approved by Legal Services and must be included in the Invitation to Tender.
note: The bond must be in a form approved by Legal Services and be included in the Invitation to Tender. Legal Services approves the form, in the same way the Monitoring Officer approves the form of contract in 10.2, so it is checked as the approver. Evidence: the approved bond form in the tender pack.

text: An entry of every sealing of a document shall be made and consecutively numbered in a book or electronic record to be provided for the purpose and shall be signed (including a digital signature) by the person attesting the sealing.
note: Every sealing must be entered, consecutively numbered and signed. Evidence: the sealing register.

text: Where it becomes necessary to execute any document on behalf of the Council not required by law to be under seal, the Monitoring Officer or an officer designated by them in accordance with the delegated powers conferred by the Council shall be deemed to have authority to sign such a document accordingly. A register of such documents shall be kept by the Monitoring Officer or officer duly designated by them.
note: The Monitoring Officer or a designated officer signs documents not under seal, and a register of them must be kept. Evidence: the register.

text: Above the relevant threshold and less than £500,000: Relevant Service Director (following recommendation of the S151 officer and Monitoring Officer) shall have delegated authority to award the contract provided a written report by the relevant Service Director (or such officers as nominated by them in writing) has been provided and approved by the relevant board.
note: Awards between the Threshold and £500,000: Service Director awards after S151 and Monitoring Officer recommendation, with a written report approved by the board. Lower bound is the statutory Threshold, not stated, so not checked.

text: £2.5million or more: Contracts with a value in excess of £2.5million shall require Executive approval, which may be given as below. The Executive shall receive quarterly reports detailing contracts being procured and seeking delegated authority from Executive for the relevant Service Director / to award the contract following the procurement process in consultation with the relevant Portfolio Holder, S.151 Officer and the Monitoring Officer.
note: £2.5 million or more requires Executive approval. Evidence: the Executive decision.

text: Above £1,000 and less than £25,000: At least one quote must be sought from an appropriate source. Advertising: None mandated.
note: Between £1,000 and £25,000: at least one quote. Evidence: the quote on file.

text: Goods and Services: £25,000 or more and less than the Threshold: Invitations to quote must be sent via the Procurement Portal to at least three appropriate sources, including at least one SME* or VCSE* organisation and one local supplier (where appropriate and possible). Advertising: A contract notice must be published on the CDP.
note: £25,000 up to the Threshold (goods and services): invitations to at least three sources through the Portal, and a contract notice. Upper bound is the statutory Threshold, not stated, so not checked.

text: Works, Concession contracts and Light Touch contracts: Above £500,000 and less than the Threshold: Full competitive tender process applies and at least five written tenders must be sought via the Procurement Portal. Advertising: An advert should be placed on the Portal together with information on the CDP.
note: Above £500,000 up to the Threshold (works, concession, light touch): at least five written tenders through the Portal.

text: The proposed contract is excluded under the Procurement Legislation. Written record and approval: Prior written approval from the Monitoring Officer is required and where applicable prior approval has been granted by the relevant board.
note: A contract excluded under the legislation needs the Monitoring Officer's prior written approval. Evidence: the approval, dated before award.

text: The proposed contract is an extension to an existing contract where the existing contract provides for such extension. Written record and approval: Approval of the S151 Officer.
note: An extension the contract provides for needs S151 Officer approval. Evidence: the approval.

text: The contract is for social care services (residential placements, supported living, SEN school placements, personalisation packages, specific-provider packages, Shared Lives). Written record and approval: Service Directors must ensure that a record of the reasons for the choice of provider is maintained on the individual's case notes.
note: For the listed social care placements, a record of the reasons for the choice of provider must be kept on the case notes. The Service Director is responsible for it, not an approver. Evidence: the record.
